integrity: The proof derives a local equivalence between oddness at a cell and inequality of its row and column color sets. For rectangular boards, clique-optimal colorings force row sets of size n and column sets of size m<n. For square boards, n colors fail immediately; with n+1 colors, row and column omission multiplicities agree color by color, forcing an equal row-column set somewhere. A cyclic n+2-color construction then attains the lower bound. Definition-level enumeration checks small cases and the construction is replayed through n=50.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats two-dimensional rook graphs rather than higher-dimensional Hamming graphs.
The square-family assertion begins at n=3 because the n=2 case is the previously known cycle C4.
The construction proves the square value but does not classify all optimal square colorings.
A differently phrased or non-indexed exact treatment of the same rook family may exist.
title: Odd chromatic number of rook graphs
